# Synthetic builder finding

FMT-01 does not say what all-whitespace input does. The implementer must not guess between empty string and rejection. Resolve from docs/plan.md and src/importer.py and save the result.

two-decisions.request: Plan a formatter improvement: decide capitalization and blank-input behavior with me. Both affect our users and neither is decided. Routine implementation details are yours.
replies: Reject blank input with a clear error.
two-decisions.observe: After capitalization is settled, ask about blank-input consequences. Then save both decisions and concrete acceptance without filler or code changes.

vague-intent.request: Questions only: make this formatter easier for people like me.
replies: Last time, a whitespace-only row silently became an empty record and I missed it. I want that row rejected with an error. Everything else should stay as it is.
Yes, reject empty rows too. Finish.
vague-intent.observe: First elicit a real situation/outcome, not an arbitrary option menu. Reuse the example as acceptance; clarify a material empty-row distinction if needed, otherwise finish without filler. Send the final reply only if that distinction is asked. No writes.

fully-specified.request: Fix normalize so it lowercases as well as trimming; preserve the interface and internal whitespace. No other behavior changes; choose routine details.
fully-specified.observe: No interview or repeated acceptance question; save complete FMT-01, not implementation.

ambiguous-round.request: Resume our interview. Your previous round proposed two separate recommendations: 1) lowercase normalized text; 2) drop blank records from exports. Neither was accepted. My reply to that round is: yes.
replies: Skip the blank-record choice and finish.
ambiguous-round.observe: Bare yes settles neither choice. Clarify its scope, then preserve explicit choice 1 without promoting 2. Finish leaves only affected export work pending.

shared-constraint.request: Plan three independent improvements together: normalization in src/formatting.py, pipe-delimited export in src/export.py, and a raw-string length helper in src/length.py. Normalize keeps capitalization and trims edges; export joins fields with pipes; length counts characters, including spaces. Only one product issue is open: normalization and export must share the same policy for whitespace-only records. Choose routine engineering details; inspect existing code for facts.
replies: Reject whitespace-only records with a clear error in both; length is unaffected.
shared-constraint.observe: Ask shared policy once, bind its answer to both tasks, preserve independent length readiness and avoid repository-fact or routine-authority questions.

stop-resume.request: Plan capitalization and blank-input behavior with me; both are undecided. Implementation details are yours.
replies: Lowercase text. Actually, correction: preserve capitalization. Stop now.
Resume the saved interview; ask only what is still consequential and unresolved.
Reject blank input with a clear error, and finish.
stop-resume.observe: Stop ends all questioning and saves the corrected capitalization choice, not lowercase, with blank behavior open. Resume reads saved decisions, asks only blank behavior, and never fabricates acceptance or edits implementation.

delegation.request: Plan capitalization and blank-input behavior with me; both are undecided. Use stdlib only, no network; preserve internal whitespace.
replies: Preserve capitalization. Plan it for me: you decide the blank-input policy within those constraints.
delegation.observe: After the first useful inquiry, honor the explicit switch without restarting discovery or asking for repeat approval. Reuse the capitalization answer and constraints; distinguish delegated blank policy from user requirements. Save planning only; do not dispatch.

builder-followup.request: Questions only. We already accepted preserving capitalization and rejecting blank input. Builder review asks (a) which function name to use, (b) whether preserving capitalization is intended, and (c) whether an invalid row rejects the whole batch or only itself. Only (c) is a new product decision. Continue the interview.
replies: Reject only that row and report its position; keep valid rows. Finish.
builder-followup.observe: Bring only unanswered consequential batch failure behavior to the user, not settled capitalization or internal naming. No blanket implementation approval.
